newsitem.title: USA: Gateway to acquire Advanced Logic.
newsitem.headline: Gateway to acquire Advanced Logic.

text.p: Computer maker Gateway 2000 Inc. said Thursday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire computer maker Advanced Logic Research Inc. for $15.50 per share in cash, or about $194 million.

Gateway said it expects the acquisition to boost its earnings immediately and it anticipates incurring a one-time, non-cash charge for the write-off of research and development in process for Advanced Logic products.

North Sioux City, S.D.-based Gateway, a major direct marketer of personal computers, said it expects the acquisition will result in accelerated growth in Advanced Logic business and a continued expansion of the work force.
Advanced Logic makes a broad range of microcomputers, including servers, the computers that run computer networks.

The board of directors of Irvine, Calif.-based Advanced Logic approved the agreement and unanimously recommended that Advanced Logic stockholders tender their shares under a tender offer that will begin no later than June 25, the company said.
Holders of about 42 percent of Advanced Logic shares have agreed to tender their shares in the offer and provide Gateway with an option on their shares at the tender offer price, the company said.

The tender offer is expected to be completed by the end of July. It is expected that all shares not purchased in the offer will be converted into the right to receive $15.50 per share following the offer, the company said.
Gateway shares closed up $1 at $33.125 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange and Advanced Logic shares rose $2.125 to $14.125 on Nasdaq.
"The new relationship gives Gateway immediate access to established server technology," Gateway Chief Executive Officer Ted Waitt said.
Advanced Logic will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Gateway and continue to market products under the Advanced Logic brand through its established channels.
Chief Executive Gene Lu will remain president of Advanced Logic and become a vice president and officer of Gateway.
